fact: Kenya was to begin a pilot in July 2025 of KEMIS, integrated with the national digital ID system (Maisha Namba), with full go-live set for September, as reported by Biometric Update citing The Kenya Times.

A Ministry of Education circular says the KEMIS Learner Validation Engine is operational and automatically compares learner records against official examination and assessment databases, marking learners Valid or Invalid.

The Ministry of Education unveiled a 15-member multi-agency team to build KEMIS, consolidating the separate registers for ECDE, basic education, TIVET and universities into one database, with a pilot announced for July 2025 and full transition in September, and with planned integration with the births and deaths register through Civil Registration Services and the National Registration Bureau.

Nairobi Wire reports a State House meeting of the Head of Public Service with the Public Service Commission, the Kenya National Examinations Council and the Ministry of Education to integrate the systems that authenticate academic qualifications and link credential databases directly with hiring agencies, with no technological framework or timeline disclosed.
